findings.reason: the plan must name `default_registry` (or Nova's generic registry entry point) as the owner to extend with a machine key, which is the same unowned-shared-infrastructure gap the plan closes deliberately everywhere else.
findings.text: §7 requires a JT-60SA identity registry to hand `identity_for_shot`, but the registry owner `default_registry()` returns `nova.catalog.mast_geometry.MachineGeometryRegistry.default()` and is cached to MAST alone, while §7 also insists "nothing JT-60SA-specific is added to nova"; the plan therefore leaves the JT-60SA registry unowned, so the first selection node will either fork a second registry route beside `default_registry` or silently re-use MAST's

duplicate_owner-1.reason: Acted in plan v104: section 7 extends imas_ambix/gs/machine_identity.py default_registry with a machine key, one cached registry per machine; MAST unchanged; a machine with no registry is refused by name.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the three new modules each hide substantial behaviour behind a small interface (`eddb_remote.py`: ssh transport plus batch framing plus per-channel refusal behind one batch call; `eddb.py`: cache identity, half-written detection and overwrite refusal behind `fetch_channels`/`write_channel`; `selene_deck.py`: three deck grammars plus per-phase IDS emission behind one entry point), so the additions are depth rather than surface.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §7 threads `machine` into `identity_for_shot` and refers to "the registry for the declared machine", but the identity-registry owner `gs/machine_identity.py::default_registry` is hard-wired to Nova's MAST registry and no section names the mechanism that yields a JT-60SA one.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; the one CLI addition (§7 `scripts/spine_benchmark.py --machine`) states it retires the implicit MAST default an explicit shot list carried, and each section that widens a public definition or refusal family states in its own text why nothing can be retired (§3 "ambix had no remote reader", §4 "no binding could select a struct-array entry before", §5 "no EDDB unit spelling is recorded anywhere today", §6 "every existing name keeps its caller"), so the addition is accounted for.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan searched the two codebases it names and, for each subsystem it adds, cites the existing mechanism it extends (`StoreEngine.open` gains the selected map; `read_geometry_table`'s machine branch is retired not joined; the COCOS cohort feeds `score_convention`; the equilibrium kernel is `_integrated_current` in `challenge/convention.py`; the reference seam is `read_efit_geometry`'s `loader=`), and every cited owner exists and matches the plan's account.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the only interfaces that could read as thin layers carry their justification in-text: the tokamap exporter is "kept out of the loaders because they read the ambix schema and must not learn tokamap's", the EQDB reader extends `RemoteEddbExtractor` because "only the remote read call differs", and the EQDB record writer sits in `eddb.py` to share the store invariants rather than restate them.
